cards.title: Step 1 · Musical style — Christopher's own direction
cards.prompt:
Christopher chose none of the three (via Telegram, 3:38 PM): "something more like the musical style in Monolith, The Resonance Chamber or When the Wires Wake, with the artistic style of Monolith."

Sound: Dark industrial electronica and cinematic darksynth in the family of Monolith (Horizon), The Resonance Chamber (Horizon) and When the Wires Wake (Astra): a heavy half-time stride, saturated detuned analog sub-bass, dry crushing kick, cavernous snare, ticking metallic percussion, cold granular pads, and a low, intimate voice inside the machinery. Original melody and lyric; none of those recordings are used.

Art: Monolith's look: monochrome architectural pen-and-ink, brutalist megastructures, cables and conduits as the performers, a small human figure for scale; charcoal, slate and bone paper with one restrained accent colour. New plates only; none of Monolith's art is used.

Tempo: about 138 BPM, felt as a 69 BPM half-time stride.
Suno style line for step 4: dark industrial electronica, cinematic darksynth, 138 bpm half-time stride, saturated detuned analog sub-bass, dry crushing kick, cavernous snare, ticking metallic percussion, cold granular pads, low intimate baritone vocal, minor key, vast negative space, nocturnal

options.name: Desert Night Soul (not chosen)
options.description: Slow-burning cinematic desert blues: tremolo baritone guitar, frame drum and hand claps, upright bass, a smoky low female vocal; the last chorus opens into a wide, gospel-tinged group answer. Feeling: Heat leaving the sand after dark. Patient, a little dangerous, then warm. Tempo: about 72 BPM, half-time swing.

options.name: Harbor Lights City Pop (not chosen)
options.description: Bright 1980s-style city pop: slap bass, Rhodes piano, glassy chorus guitar, short brass stabs, a light male–female duet trading lines and meeting on the hook. Feeling: A late ferry ride into a lit-up harbor, windows down, nothing urgent. Tempo: about 112 BPM, steady four-on-the-floor lift in the chorus.

options.name: Cathedral Breaks (not chosen)
options.description: Starts as a still choir over an organ drone and bells, then drops into fast, liquid drum and bass: rolling breakbeats, deep sub, chopped choir phrases over the top. Feeling: Stone and stained glass suddenly running. Awe that turns into motion. Tempo: slow, free intro, then 172 BPM.

options.name: Load-Bearing
options.description:
A lone keeper deep inside a megastructure is the wall everyone leans on without knowing. Tender, unthanked, steady.
Hook: Load-bearing, load-bearing — I am the wall you lean on in the dark.
Chorus: Ten thousand floors above my head / and every one of them asleep / I hum the cables, warm the steel / I keep the promise that I keep / Load-bearing, load-bearing / I don't need you to know my name / just lean a little on the dark / and I will hold you all the same
Refrain: Hold… hold… the city holds.

options.name: The Hundredth Dark
options.description:
A descent through level after empty level, looking for the bottom of the structure, and of a feeling. Letting go as relief.
Hook: Take me down to the hundredth dark.
Chorus: Past the furnace, past the floodgate / past the rooms with no one in / every level colder, quieter / every door I close again / Take me down to the hundredth dark / where the last lamp never reached / if there's nothing at the bottom / I can finally stop and breathe
Refrain: Down… and down… and down… and still.

options.name: Concrete Remembers
options.description:
The building remembers everyone who ever passed through it. Ghosts held in architecture; nothing is lost, only stored.
Hook: The concrete remembers your weight.
Chorus: You walked these halls a hundred years ago / your footsteps poured into the floor / the stone kept every word you said / it kept the shape of every door / The concrete remembers your weight / the girders remember your hand / everything you built is still awake / still waiting for you to stand
Refrain: Nothing here forgets.

cards.title: Step 3 · Choose the artistic world
cards.prompt: Three takes on Monolith's monochrome ink style, each drawn around 'the concrete remembers your weight'. Choose on the phone page (saves work now) or reply with a letter. If nothing's chosen by 4:15, I'll pick and say so (the lyric and style go to Suno then; the world matters from step 6).

options.name: Bone & Ember
options.description: Dry, monumental halls drawn in black ink on bone paper. Footprints of everyone who ever walked here are pressed into the concrete floor; a few ember-orange lamps burn in doorways. Closest to Monolith's stark ink.
options.imageAlt: Ink drawing of vast brutalist concrete galleries, a lone figure on a pale floor marked with trails of old footprints, small ember-orange lamps in doorways.

options.name: Rain & Sodium
options.description: Ink with grey wash: it rains inside a colossal atrium, and the silhouettes of past residents still stand in the windows. One sodium-yellow doorway reflects in the flooded floor. Wetter, sadder, more cinematic.
options.imageAlt: Grey ink-wash drawing of rain inside a towering concrete atrium, faint figures in the windows, a figure with an umbrella before a yellow-lit doorway reflected in water.

options.name: Blueprint Negative
options.description: The building as its own memory: white line on blue-black, a tower cut open in section, every room and stairwell still holding the people who lived there, a warm light at its heart. The most graphic and the most literal take on 'the concrete remembers'.
options.imageAlt: White-line drawing on dark blue paper of a tower cut open in section, many small figures in its rooms and stairwells, a warm glow at the centre.
